title: Kafka: topics, partitions, offsets and retention

videos.script: In the last lesson the log was one file, written by one program. Kafka keeps the same idea and spreads it out. {{one-file}} A topic is a name. Under the name are partitions, and each partition is a log of its own, with its own offsets, starting at zero. {{partitions}} The producer decides which partition a message goes to. It hashes the key, so every sale from Recife lands in the same place, in order. {{hash}} But two clients can hash the same key differently. You will watch a Python program and Kafka's own tool put Recife in different partitions. {{surprise}} Then you open the files on disk. A partition is a row of segments, each with an index beside it. {{segments}} And a log cannot grow forever. Kafka deletes old segments when they are too old or too big, or keeps only the last value for each key. {{retention}} By the end you will know where every message is, and how long it stays there. {{end}}
